title: Agentic AI Risk Evaluation Should Become a Continuous Assurance Discipline
content: Language-model agents act through tools and credentials. A score from one tested configuration should not keep authorizing actions after the system, permissions, or threat model change. We argue that agentic AI is the first high-stakes domain in which assurance-invalidating change routinely outpaces evidence renewal. Continuous assurance is therefore not an improvement on benchmark evaluation, but a precondition for an authorization claim being true when it is relied upon. The machinery exists in nuclear, aviation, and medical-device regulation. Three requirements do not: a configuration baseline that makes change detectable, a change taxonomy calibrated to hazard relevance, and qualification criteria for evaluation environments. We propose the Agentic Assurance Stack (Stack), a versioned assurance profile linking each action path to a bounded claim, five evidence obligations, and a renewal rule.
